transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
Hi. Um... I guess I'm here because I just feel like I'm always running hot. Like I can't shut the motor off. And... well, it's been getting me in trouble at the firehouse lately. So, yeah.
When you say you can't shut the motor off, have there been times in your life when you felt completely normal and calm, or has this always been pretty much how you are?

Uh... I don't really remember being calm, no. I guess it's pretty much always been this way. 

My mom says I was like this back in grade school, too. Just... always getting out of my seat. Blurting answers out. I'd lose my homework a lot, get notes sent home... even though they said I was bright enough to do the work. So... yeah. Always like this.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F32.9, F33.9, F31.9, F41.9, F60.3, F60.8. Patient presents with lifelong hyperactivity, impulsivity (blurting answers), inattention (losing homework), and early-onset symptoms in grade school. This is classic ADHD presentation, not mood disorder, anxiety disorder, or personality disorder. F90.9 (ADHD, unspecified) is the clear diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with lifelong symptoms of hyperactivity-impulsivity (can't shut the motor off, always running hot, getting out of seat, blurting answers) with onset in childhood (grade school), chronic course, and current functional impairment (getting in trouble at firehouse). Symptoms are pervasive across settings and time. No clear inattention symptoms were explicitly detailed during interview, though homework loss could suggest organizational difficulties. The predominantly hyperactive-impulsive presentation with lifelong course and childhood onset meets criteria for ADHD, unspecified type (F90.9), though F90.1 (hyperkinetic disorder) and F90.0 (disturbance of activity and attention) remain differential considerations pending more detailed assessment of inattention.
